messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Converting a JAGS model to Stan.
parts:
Hi,

The dimensions of Temp (and some of your other local variables) look way off.

As written, Temp is a 1058x1058x1058x1058 4-way array (tensor) with
approximately 1.3*10^{12} elements. At 8 bytes per element, simply
allocating the memory for it would take about 9 TB of memory, hence
the error. From your JAGS code, it looks like the dimensions of Temp
should be something closer to 2x3x3x3. (You assign to N=20, but you
only use three values for the second coordinate). It may be that JAGS
only instantiates the slices that actually get written to (haven't
used it enough to know), but Stan actually allocates the memory
(unless you use sparse structures).

If N only ever takes values 8, 14, 20: I would declare [8, 14, 20] as
an array and then use for(i in 1:3) loops for indexing. When you
actually need the values, then just use N[i] instead (but as far as I
can tell, 8, 14, 20 are just labels: they never actually get used as
values in your code)

Michael
